correctness.rationale: For the specified diagonal integral Lie ring [h,v_j]=a_j v_j with positive integer a_j and gcd1, the Chevalley–Eilenberg dual basis has d(alpha)=0, d(beta_S)=−w(S)alpha∧beta_S, and d(alpha∧beta_S)=0, with w(S)=Σ_{j∈S}a_j>0. The integral cochain complex splits explicitly into Z in degrees 0/1 with zero differential plus one rank-one map multiplication by w(S) for every nonempty S. Therefore H^0=H^1=Z and H^{k>=2}=⊕_{|S|=k-1}Z/w(S), positive-degree products vanish because surviving classes carry alpha. Reduction mod p yields c_k(p)+c_{k−1}(p) dimensions, primes exceptional iff dividing a positive subset sum; with weights (1,m), H²=Z/m,H³=Z/(m+1). The positive-weight hypothesis rules out zero maps over Z. Independent subset-sum and modular calculations checked six representative weight multisets and several primes. This is Lie-ring CE cohomology, not group cohomology.

value.rationale: A natural full integral cohomological invariant for the canonical positive-weight diagonal form of the recently classified almost-abelian family. The complete arithmetic torsion decomposition and exceptional-prime description, including arbitrarily large coprime consecutive torsion orders already in dimension three, are specific facts not supplied by the known field-cohomology statement. The proof is elementary but the invariant and normalized family are motivated, so shortness alone does not make the exact structural classification worthless.

limitations: Specified free Z-Lie ring with normalized positive diagonal integral weights, not general almost abelian integral forms.
